newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia mulling rouble-dollar peg in 1997 - C.Bank.
newsitem.headline: Russia mulling rouble-dollar peg in 1997 - C.Bank.

text.p: The Russian central bank is considering pegging the rouble in a tight range against the dollar or another convertible currency next year because it fears the present system could be inflationary.
A document prepared by the bank for the State Duma lower house of parliament said today's lower inflation rates meant that a pegged currency rate could be possible.
"The low inflation rate we have achieved in 1996 (about 24 annual), will allow us to consider a fixed currency rate as an alternative in 1997," said the document.
The rouble would be allowed to move within a narrow band allowing fluctuation of four or five percent, it said.

But the bank stressed fixed rates were only one of the options. The bank could also continue the current policy of a "sloping corridor", which sets daily target ranges and allows the rouble to fall gently each day.
A third alternative would be to change the rouble's target range a few times each year.
The central bank said continuing the sloping corridor would result in a rouble-dollar rate of 6,200 roubles per dollar by the end of 1997. The currency traded at around 5,440 on Friday.
But allowing the rouble to fall at rates like these could encourage faster inflation, the central bank said.
"The central bank thinks it expedient to provide for the possibility of quarterly rate corrections within annual hard currency limits," the report said.
